If you’re looking around Birmingham, I’d start with the **Royal Kennel Club’s puppy listings** rather than choosing a breeder solely from Facebook or classified ads. Its current Staffordshire Bull Terrier search shows a **blue litter in Smethwick**, among other UK listings, and lets you filter for health-tested parents. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

A couple of local listings also show up:

- Staffy Society UK — Quinton, Birmingham.
- Staffy Puppies for Sale UK — Sutton Coldfield.

I would **verify their current litters and health documentation before paying a deposit**; a business listing by itself isn't evidence that a breeder is responsible.

### What to ask the breeder

For a Staffy, I'd specifically ask:

- **Can I see the mother with the puppies?** Ideally see where the puppies were raised, not just a puppy handed over somewhere else.
- **Can I see the father's details and health certificates too?**
- **Are both parents DNA-tested clear for L-2-HGA and hereditary cataracts (HC-HSF4)?** These are specifically recommended health tests for Staffordshire Bull Terriers. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club](https://www.northerncountiesstaffordshirebullterrierclub.co.uk/Code-Of-Ethics.php?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Have the parents had eye testing and elbow screening?** The Royal Kennel Club also recommends BVA/KC eye testing and elbow dysplasia screening as part of its breed-specific health guidance. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **What are the parents' Kennel Club registration names/numbers?** You can then independently check their health-test results and pedigree.
- **What is the parents' COI (coefficient of inbreeding)?** Ask them to show you the actual figure rather than simply saying "low COI."
- **How old is the mother, and how many litters has she had?**
- **What vaccinations, microchipping and worming has the puppy received?**
- **What food is the puppy currently eating, and what routine/socialisation has it had?**
- **Will you provide a contract and take the puppy back if I can no longer keep it?**
- **Can I contact you after purchase if I have health or behavioural questions?**

### One important point about "blue"

Blue is **a recognised Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour** under the current Royal Kennel Club standard, so there's nothing inherently wrong with wanting a blue Staffy. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/breed-standards/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

However, don't let the colour become the main selling point. The Royal Kennel Club explicitly says **health and temperament should take priority over colour**. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

I'd also be wary of anyone advertising a puppy primarily with phrases such as *"rare blue," "XXL," "micro," "exotic"* or claiming that an unusual appearance makes it especially valuable.

**Before paying anything**, ask the breeder to send you copies/photos of the parents' actual health-test results and their KC details. If you give me your **rough radius from Birmingham (e.g. 20, 40 or 60 miles)** and whether you want a **dog or bitch**, I can search the current listings and narrow it down to blue Staffy litters worth contacting.
